title: ID Churn Sentinel evidence bundle manifest v1
description: The manifest at the root of a portable evidence bundle: the raw bytes, normalized texts, contract versions, fetch receipts and re-derivable diff behind ONE published change, packaged so a third party can check the claim without the operator's store, the operator's network, or the operator's word. Written by `sentinel evidence export <change-id> --out DIR`; re-checked by `sentinel evidence verify DIR`, which recomputes every hash listed here, refuses any file this manifest does not list, re-runs normalization under the recorded contract version, re-derives the diff, and confirms the bytes hash to the values the published change record cites. Bundles are not signed: the signing trust model is SEC-03/ENG-06 and deliberately out of scope here.

exported_at.description: When the bundle was written. NOT when the change was observed, and never used as evidence about the source.

previous_hash.description: The detection hash of the baseline, exactly as the published change record carries it. `verify` recomputes this from before/raw.bin under the recorded hashing regime; that recomputation is the bundle's tie to the feed.

sides.description: The two retained snapshots. A bundle always carries both: export refuses, and writes nothing, when either has been pruned out of the store.

published_excerpt_is_rederivable.description: MEASURED at export time, not asserted: the exporter re-derives the published excerpt from the two normalized texts and records whether it came out identical. It does not when the excerpt carries a re-normalization provenance note or hit its character budget, neither of which is a function of the two texts alone. When false, `verify` reports the published-excerpt check as SKIPPED with `published_excerpt_note` as the reason — it does not fail an honest bundle, and it does not report a pass for a check it never ran.

published_excerpt_note.description: Why the excerpt is not re-derivable. Empty when it is.

files.description: Every file in the bundle except this manifest, with its SHA-256 and length. `verify` fails on the FIRST listed file whose bytes disagree, naming it — and separately fails on any file present in the directory that is not listed here, because an unlisted file is verified by nothing and read by whoever opens the handover.

hashing_regime.description: Which regime produced `content_sha256`. Text and HTML are hashed over the normalized text; anything binary is hashed over the raw bytes, losslessly, so a change the extractor cannot read still moves the hash. Derived at export by finding which regime reproduces the stored hash — never assumed.

content_type.description: The Content-Type the body was read under, taken from the fetch receipt that recorded these exact bytes. Required: without it a verifier cannot re-run normalization, and export refuses rather than shipping bytes nobody can re-derive.

representation_contract.description: The two versions as one contract string. `verify` FAILS CLOSED, naming the version, when this build does not implement it: re-deriving under a different normalizer and reporting agreement would be worse than reporting nothing.

http_status.description: The status the fetch returned, or null when the store recorded none. Null is an absence and is never rendered as a status.

path.description: Bundle-relative, POSIX-separated. Never absolute and never traversing upward.
